decisions.descriptionMarkdown:
release-plz is the only release tool, in git-only mode (`git_only = true`, `publish = false`: versions come from tags, nothing reaches a registry). On every push to `main` `.github/workflows/release-plz.yml` runs `release-pr` (keeps a release PR with the next `[workspace.package] version`, `Cargo.lock` and the new `CHANGELOG.md` section) and `release` (tags `v{{ version }}` and creates the GitHub Release when the version in `Cargo.toml` has no tag: a merged release PR or the initial `1.0.0`). The workflow is the CLI's, guarded by `github.repository == 'rayx-ui/RayX.Reactive'` and authenticated with `RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN`, so the release PR starts `ci.yml`.

One released package: `rayx_reactive` (in `crates/`) owns the tag, the Release and the root changelog (`changelog_path = "./CHANGELOG.md"`); `rayx_reactive_doc_examples` has `release = false`; no `version_group`/`changelog_include`. `release_commits` and `semver_check` follow `d-one-x-policy`. `[changelog]` is the CLI's git-cliff configuration naming `rayx_reactive` (plus the migration line of `d-changelog-from-commits`).
decisions.invariantsMarkdown:
- Tags have the form `v<semver>`, come only from release-plz or the documented by-hand fallback, and are never moved or deleted (the "Release tags" ruleset enforces it).
- `RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN` is the only release secret; it lives in GitHub Actions only.
- `release-plz.yml` runs no tests.
- Nothing is published to crates.io; the manifests stay crates.io-ready (`cargo package --workspace` passes).
- One released package, one `v*` tag per release, one root `CHANGELOG.md`; `doc-examples` is never versioned or released.
decisions.rationaleMarkdown: Owner decisions of 2026-10-18 (git tags, start at 1.0.0, one shared PAT, the CLI as model, release-plz creating the GitHub Release for libraries). `changelog_path` is needed because release-plz otherwise writes `crates/CHANGELOG.md` next to the package manifest. Evidence that git-only first releases need no PR: RayX.CLI's first Release-plz run (2026-10-14) logged "No release tag found ... treated as initial release", "next version is 1.0.0", "already up-to-date" in `release-pr`, and "released rayx-cli 1.0.0 (git-only)" in `release`. The single-crate decision's goal of a library "publishable on its own" stays true: the package keeps passing `cargo package`; it is released through tags instead of a registry.

decisions.descriptionMarkdown: The crate stays on 1.x.x while the owner is its only consumer (owner, amendment 1, 2026-10-18). release-plz cannot cap a major bump: it bumps the major for a `!` commit, a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer, or an API break cargo-semver-checks reports. So: `release_commits = "^(feat|fix|perf)"`; `semver_check = false`; commits are never marked breaking; a breaking change is committed as `feat` (minor), or `fix` when it is a fix, with the break stated in the body and the consumer note in a `Migration:` footer. Before a release PR is merged, its proposed version must still be 1.x; a `2.0.0` proposal means a stray `!`/`BREAKING CHANGE:`, and that commit is reworded (force push allowed) instead of merging. `docs/releasing.md` and `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` state the policy and that it ends when a second consumer appears; then `!`, major bumps and the semver check return.
decisions.invariantsMarkdown:
- Every proposed or released version is 1.x.
- No commit after `v1.0.0` carries `!` or a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer.
- `semver_check = false` and `release_commits = "^(feat|fix|perf)"`, each commented with the policy.
decisions.rationaleMarkdown: Replaces the original plan's broadened `release_commits` (any breaking type) and its experiment on `semver_check` in git-only mode; both only mattered for major bumps, which the policy rules out (release-plz.dev/docs/semver-check: "When release-plz detects API breaking changes, it updates the version of the package with a major semver bump"). The pre-1.0 history keeps its `!` commits; preview A proves they do not affect the initial release.

decisions.descriptionMarkdown:
From 1.0.0 on, commits are the changelog. `CHANGELOG.md` starts with exactly the configured `[changelog] header` (git-cliff strips that string from the old file and writes header + new section + rest), followed by release sections `## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD`, newest first. The existing hand-written `Unreleased` notes become the `## [1.0.0]` section unchanged, with the old "unpublished (0.1)" sentence reworded into its lead line; release-plz reads that section as the body of the `v1.0.0` GitHub Release.

The repository's *Migration:* convention survives under the 1.x policy: the commit carries a `Migration: <note>` footer, and one additive line in the CLI's body template renders `*Migration:* {{ footer.value }}` under the entry for each footer in `commit.footers` whose token is `Migration`. Between releases nobody edits `CHANGELOG.md`; wording fixes happen in the release PR before it is merged. `[workspace.package] version` becomes `1.0.0` (inherited by `rayx_reactive`), `Cargo.lock` follows, `doc-examples` keeps `0.0.0`.
decisions.invariantsMarkdown:
- `CHANGELOG.md` begins with the configured header byte for byte; there is never an `Unreleased` section.
- Every breaking change carries a migration note in its `Migration:` footer.
- At promotion: the CHANGELOG clause of `knowledge/repository/rules.md` changes from "record every change in CHANGELOG.md" to "commits are the changelog; a breaking change is a `feat`/`fix` with a `Migration:` footer, never `!`"; `knowledge/repository/state.md` drops "version 0.1.0 ... published to crates.io" for "1.0.0, released as git tags by release-plz under the 1.x policy".
decisions.rationaleMarkdown: The 1.0.0 section is the most valuable release note the crate has (eleven migration notes for RayX), so it is kept verbatim instead of regenerated. A header mismatch would duplicate the header on the first release PR; preview B proves the prepend on this exact file. The template line keeps the repository rule without a manual edit per release PR; it is the only deviation from the CLI's template, and preview C proves it renders.

decisions.descriptionMarkdown: `ci.yml` keeps running on `pull_request` and on pushes to `main` (amendment 1 B); its job set stays. A release PR runs that light set once on exactly the content that will be tagged, and each push to `main` (direct pushes and release-PR merges) runs it next to `release-plz.yml`, which runs no tests and does not wait for it.
decisions.invariantsMarkdown:
- `ci.yml` keeps its `push` trigger to `main`; `release-plz.yml` runs no tests.
- `ci.yml` runs no benchmarks, e2e or device lanes; no path filter.
decisions.rationaleMarkdown: The brief asks to narrow release-PR CI only if it would start heavy suites (e2e, perf, platform matrices). `ci.yml` is a small library's standard set: six hosted jobs, no benchmarks run (Criterion benches are only compiled by Clippy), no browser, GPU or device work; its OS spread backs the README's platform table. Amendment 1 B overrides the original plan, which dropped the push trigger to make `release-plz.yml` the only push workflow.

decisions.descriptionMarkdown: The crate is consumed only by release tag: `rayx_reactive = { git = "https://github.com/rayx-ui/RayX.Reactive", tag = "vX.Y.Z" }`, latest tag from the Releases page, `Cargo.lock` recording the commit. README `Installation` and `docs/02-getting-started.md` say so and drop the crates.io promise and the path co-development snippet. `docs/releasing.md` is the maintainer document (flow, 1.x policy, token, fallback, ruleset, push policy), linked from the README and `docs/20-contributing.md`; it holds no Rust blocks. `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` get a short identical `## Releases` section, and the `rayx-reactive` skill's changelog guidance follows `d-changelog-from-commits`.
decisions.invariantsMarkdown:
- Every documented dependency form names a release tag.
- `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` stay identical.
- Rust blocks in README and `docs/*.md` keep compiling in `doc-examples`.
decisions.rationaleMarkdown: Owner decisions 1, 2 and 6: tags not crates.io, consumers pin tags, no local-override mechanism. `docs/02-getting-started.md` repeats the README's install section (found during planning), so both change. The README's tag line will name an older tag after later releases; the text says to use the latest tag instead of being rewritten per release.

decisions.descriptionMarkdown: The first release is a push, not a PR: when the push that brings `1.0.0` and `release-plz.yml` lands on `main` and no `v*` tag exists, the `release` job tags `v1.0.0` and creates the GitHub Release. The owner already created the secret and the rulesets and pre-approved the push (amendment 1 C, D), so the sprint verifies the settings, pushes all epic commits in one force-with-lease push (changelog dated that day), checks the Release-plz run, the Release, the absence of a release PR, the tag commit and `ci.yml`'s green push run, and finally lets a scratch consumer outside the repository resolve `tag = "v1.0.0"` and run a test against it. A checkout/push failure of the run means the shared PAT lacks this repository: report it to the owner and re-run only after the fix. A release-plz failure to cut the first tag uses the by-hand fallback with the owner's go-ahead.
decisions.invariantsMarkdown:
- Nothing of this epic reaches `origin/main` before task t08.
- No tag is created, moved or deleted by hand unless the owner approves the fallback; settings are verified, never created.
decisions.rationaleMarkdown: An earlier push of the workflow without the version would tag `v0.1.0`. The PAT was created for "only RayX.CLI"; whether its access was extended is unknown until the first run. The consumer check proves what RayX's switch epic will rely on, without touching RayX.
